directAnswer: To update a passkey, access your account settings where passkeys are managed, and follow the prompts to modify or replace the existing passkey.
summary: Updating a passkey involves accessing account settings and following the specific prompts for your platform.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.body: Passkeys are a secure method for authentication. Keeping them updated is crucial for maintaining account security.

sections.heading: Platform-Specific Steps
sections.body: The steps to update a passkey can vary depending on the platform you are using.

sections.heading: Common Issues
sections.body: Users may encounter difficulties if they forget their current passkey or if the platform's interface has changed.

steps.title: Access Account Settings
steps.detail: Log in to your account and navigate to the security or account settings section. This may vary by platform.

steps.title: Locate Passkey Management
steps.detail: Find the option for managing passkeys. This may be labeled as 'Passkeys', 'Security Keys', or similar.

steps.title: Update Passkey
steps.detail: Follow the prompts to update your passkey. You may need to enter the current passkey and then create a new one.

steps.title: Save Changes
steps.detail: Ensure you save any changes made to your passkey settings before exiting the account settings.

faqs.question: What if I forget my current passkey?
faqs.answer: If you forget your current passkey, look for a recovery option on your platform, or contact customer support for assistance.

faqs.question: Can I use the same passkey for multiple accounts?
faqs.answer: It's not recommended to use the same passkey across multiple accounts for security reasons.

faqs.question: How often should I update my passkey?
faqs.answer: It's advisable to update your passkey regularly, at least every few months, or immediately if you suspect any security breach.

caveats: The steps may vary slightly depending on the platform and its version.
Ensure you have access to your current passkey before attempting to update it.
